terms.comment: Classically a parasol (Mart., Juv.), as Morgan–Owens notes.

phrases.english: Take your umbrella; it’s going to rain, I think.

phrases.latin: Accipe quae nimiōs vincant umbrācula sōlēs: sit licet et ventus, tē tua vēla tegent.
phrases.english: Take a sunshade to beat the too-hot sun: even if there is wind, your awning will cover you.

sources: Lewis & Short: umbella
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. umbrella.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 399.
